$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §12 (which DECLINES to define a projection at all, on Workbench rule 8) and docs/history/10-V11-SCOPE.md §4 (the four laws this artifact is built to satisfy instead). Written from crates/ethos-parser-core/src/html.rs. A PROJECTION, not the record: the representation is the evidence, this is derived from it and is deliberately lossy, and `coverage` is where it says how. SECOND projection, deliberately not a rendering of the first — see `html_rule`.
title: ethos.html.v1
description: An HTML projection of a DocumentRepresentation, carried TOGETHER WITH the Anchor Map that inverts it back to representation nodes, a coverage census of every source character that did not reach it, and a second census of the structure the projection could not carry (v1.1-S4). It obeys the same four laws as `ethos.markdown.v1` and exists for one reason that artifact cannot serve: GFM has no `rowspan`, so the Markdown projection must expand a merged cell and count the slots that costs, while `<td rowspan>` carries the merge the document actually drew. The consumer's rule is one line: a quote that touches a `syntax` byte is not invertible.

parser_version.description: The engine build that produced this artifact.

profile_sha256.description: Hash of the pinned configuration profile. Two artifacts are comparable if and only if this matches — and since v1.1-S4 the profile carries `html_rule` beside `markdown_rule`, so a run under a different projection rule is correctly non-comparable.

source_sha256.description: Digest of the original source bytes, carried through from the representation.

representation_sha256.description: Digest of the representation this projects. The binding that makes the map checkable: without it, a map could name node ids from a different parse of a different file and read exactly the same.

html_rule.description:
Version id of the projection rule. `html-blocks-v4` (v2.2-S0) emits `

`, `

`-`

` from a PDF structure tree or an EPUB's own XHTML element name and from nowhere else — never from a font size, `
    `/`
  • ` from a tagged `/L`, and `` with the document's merges carried as `rowspan`/`colspan`. A cell is a ``, the rows below in a ``. No detector reads `/TH`, so a header anywhere else would be invented. SEPARATE from `markdown_rule` and it moves independently — a change to how a `
    `, and a header is written only where a table's own spans say one is there (decision #99): a cell spanning columns, divided by the row under it into cells that span no rows, heads a column group, and those two rows are `` in a `
    ` is spelled is not a change to how a GFM row is. Source bytes are ENTITY-ENCODED: `&`, `<` and `>` come out as `&`, `<`, `>`, the whole entity sits inside the `source` segment because `<` contains no `<` to label, and inverting a source segment therefore means HTML-unescaping it — a total, lossless transform. The census counts the CHARACTERS the document drew, not the bytes the entity took.

html.description: The HTML, as a FRAGMENT: no `<html>`, `<head>`, `<body>` or doctype, because those are bytes no document drew and the consumer's framing is theirs to choose. NEVER emitted without `anchor_map`: they are fields of one artifact rather than two files, because a companion file is a thing a pipeline strips and a field is not.

anchor_map.description: The map from `html` bytes back to evidence. Its segments TOTAL-TILE the string: sorted, contiguous, no overlap, no gap, covering 0..len(html) exactly. A map with a hole is worse than no map, because the hole is exactly where an unquotable byte hides — so an incomplete map is a hard error on both construction and parse, never a warning.

kind.description: TWO values for the engine's bytes, deliberately. `source` inverts to canonical node text; `syntax` is markup the exporter invented. There is no third for them — a 'probably source' would be the confidence field docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9 forbids, and would put the consumer back to guessing whether a quote is citable. `proposed` is no such third: it is a drafting model's text, never the engine's reading, written only where the record holds an `assist` key (decision #147), and a quote touching it is not citable, as one touching `syntax` is not.

start.description: First UTF-8 BYTE offset into `html`, inclusive. Bytes rather than characters, and the description says so: every language's slice takes one or the other, and saying which is the difference between a map and a hint.

node_ids.description: The representation nodes these bytes came from, in emission order. Present on `source` and ABSENT on `syntax`, because syntax came from no node. Never a newly minted id: a projection that invented identifiers would be a second record of one document, and two records drift. On `proposed`, exactly one: the `m`-numbered block of the record's `assist` key the bytes came from, which is no node.

coverage.description: A census, not a summary. `source_chars_emitted + source_chars_dropped == source_chars_in_representation`, asserted in CI on real fixtures. Counted in CHARACTERS of node text, because the thing being conserved is the text the representation offered.

source_chars_in_representation.description: Sum of the character count of every node's text in the representation — the RAW text, not its normalization, so that whitespace the projection collapsed is visible as a bucket rather than hidden by moving the denominator.

source_chars_emitted.description: Characters that landed in a `source` segment.

source_chars_dropped.description: Characters that did not, summed over `dropped`.

dropped.description: Where the dropped characters went, by named class, sorted by code. Checklist A14: if something is removed, the artifact says so AND says how much. 'Some content was omitted' is not a disclosure; `annotation-text-not-projected-v1: 37` is.

structural_erasures.description: Structure the projection flattened, by named class, sorted by code. On this artifact it is almost always EMPTY, and that is the point of having two projections: the `gfm-*` codes name things GFM cannot say, and HTML says them. The one exception is `gfm-list-item-run-joins-v1` — two sibling `/LI`s have identical role paths, so where the file leaves a body unnumbered nothing in the representation distinguishes 'the rest of this item' from 'the next item' and BOTH projections must guess (decision #128). Its `gfm-` prefix is historical: the erasure belongs to the tagged tree, and it carries the name of the slice that first met it.

code.description: `gfm-span-slots-unrepresentable-v1` — slots a merged cell covered that GFM cannot say it covered, `rowspan × colspan - 1` summed over the table's cells. `gfm-row-zero-separator-v1` — once per GFM table, because the delimiter row makes row 0 a header on every renderer and no detector reads `/TH`. `gfm-cell-run-claimed-twice-v1` — a run two cells both claimed, emitted under the first so that one node's characters are not counted twice. `gfm-cell-not-placed-v1` — a cell outside the declared grid or on a taken slot; its runs still project, as paragraphs. `gfm-table-not-projected-v1` — a table with zero rows or columns, or a DOCX table no run is in (decision #136). `layout-table-as-blocks-v1` — a DOCX layout table, one with a cell holding two paragraphs or more with text, or holding a nested table, written as the blocks it holds in document order rather than as a grid (decision #136); its `tables[]` record stays. `gfm-list-item-run-joins-v1` — a body run appended to an already-open list item where the file leaves either run's element unnumbered, or where a body set no lower than the open run's line follows a marker drawn in the `/LI` itself or reads on, opening lowercase with no label of its own, as a column break carries a bullet on: the boundary a role path cannot settle, since two sibling `/LI`s share one (decision #128). `mcid-run-joins-v1` — two runs the document placed in one marked-content sequence, emitted as one block, so the boundary between them is gone. `baseline-run-joins-abutted-v1` and `baseline-run-joins-spaced-v1` — the same erasure with no declaration behind it: two runs drawn as the next ink along one baseline, joined on this engine's geometry rather than the producer's word. The two are counted apart because the abutted form asserts one word and the spaced form only reproduces a space the page drew. `layout-unit-line-joins-v1` — two lines of one heading the PDF reader set in one layout unit (decision #38), joined with one space; the unit is this engine's measure, so it is counted apart from both. Decision #65 counts a label's next line in its unit here too, kept as a line break in the label's block; decisions #81 and #85 count here a bold line read on to the bold line above, #85's on a tagged page, which has no units, where its column wrapped it or it opens lowercase. `heading-number-joins-v1` — a heading's section number or marker joined to the title it opens across the gap the page set between them on one line (decision #65), with one space; the licence is the heading rule's line and the number's shape, so it is counted apart from all three. `layout-unit-gap-joins-v1` — runs of one layout unit on one line joined across the gap between them (decision #68), with one space: a page that places its words by moving its pen draws no space, and each word was a block of its own; the licence is the units rule's reading, so it is counted apart from the baseline joins. `block-element-run-joins-v1` — runs one block element of the structure tree holds, a paragraph, a heading, a list item or a cell, joined across a change of marked-content sequence (decision #84): along a line with a space only where the page drew one, onto the element's next line with a line break since decision #126, or one space in a heading, on a line its column wrapped, from bold onto bold unless the second is a label ending in `:`, or before a line Markdown would read as a block of its own; the licence is the element rather than one sequence, so it is counted apart from `mcid-run-joins-v1`. A list item's runs one numbered element holds count here too, in a sequence or across them (decision #128). So do a DOCX paragraph's runs, which its `<w:p>` holds, joined with the tab, line break or space it holds between them or with nothing (decision #130). `list-items-inferred-from-markers-v1` — not a flattening but the opposite, counted here because it is structure the projection asserts beyond the record: with `--infer-lists` alone (decision #138), a list item written for each layout unit of a document that declares no author structure opening with a list marker — a bullet, or a number of up to three digits or one letter closed by `.` or `)` — where two such units or more stand in a row, the marker kept as the page drew it after the item syntax, nested by where it stands against the items open before it; the item holds the rest of its unit, those joins counted under the two `layout-unit-*` codes. Inferred, not declared: the representation is unchanged and carries no list. Absent without the option. `tables-joined-across-pages-v1` — a table written as the rest of the one before it, once per join (decision #142): it stands on the next page, read off the page's ink or text as the first was and after it in `tables[]`, with as many columns, the pages of one size and turn; between them only running heads and folios another page repeats at the same side and place, `/Artifact`s, blank runs, annotations and form fields, never an inferred heading, under one running head and one running foot (digits and all, but a folio in the foot), and no picture below the first or above the second that no other page repeats at its place; the first reaching, within the second's first row under its header, the lowest point the document's body reaches on a page of its height; and the second's first row repeating the first's header cell for cell — where an author's tree cites either, only the tree's own header cells, inside a `/TR`, cited again on the second page say so. A continuation that does not repeat its header stays a table of its own. The record keeps both tables; the rows of the second follow the first's.

count.description: How many. Never a severity and never a ratio (docs/01-CONTRACT.md §9). Only non-zero classes appear: a list of codes all reading `0` is the disclosure-shaped noise a reader learns to skip, and every code is documented here whether or not a document trips it.

proposed.description:
What this artifact writes and leaves out of a drafting model's blocks (decision #147). PRESENT EXACTLY WHERE THE RECORD HOLDS AN `assist` KEY, so an engine-only artifact is byte for byte what it was. Under the rule `assist-lightonocr-v1`, a page where the engine read under 30% of the model's words (`model > 0`, `10 * shared < 3 * model`, `2 * model >= engine`, in decision #123's words: distinct runs of letters, digits and `_`, two characters or more, lower-cased, tags removed; `model` counted in the blocks a swap would write, not a cut last block, furniture `--drop-furniture` leaves out, a table's text outside its cells or a line the guard leaves out; `engine` in the engine-only Markdown) is swapped: the engine's runs and tables there are left out, counted in `coverage.dropped` under `replaced-by-proposed-page-v1`, and the model's blocks follow in reply order in one `
` opening with a `

` naming the page (`page N as read`, with `, chart values estimated` where a chart's value on it is an estimate) and the model and closing with a `

` saying `End of proposed text.`, the model's blocks between them in a `

` of their own, the model's text and name escaped, U+0000 left out. On every other page, each `table` and `chart` block, with the `title` or `caption` before it unless all its words are the engine's, is added in such a `
`, its `

` naming the table or chart and the model, a cell holding an estimate marked `data-estimate="true"` and one emptied `data-dropped="contradicted"` or `"unsupported"`, after the last run of the page that overlaps it across and starts above its foot, at the next block boundary, or before the page's first node; a model table whose cells, spans and rows equal an engine table's it overlaps on half the smaller box is left out. A model table is written from its parsed cells (a GFM grid here in Markdown, spans flattened; with its spans in HTML), never as the model's HTML, and not at all where its spans would lay it out on more than 100,000 slots (`proposed-table-unparsed-v1`); in text, tags but ``, `` and `
` are removed. The guard's `contradicted` and `unsupported` lines are left out, a cell emptied, never removed; a reply's cut last block is left out.

model.description: The model the record's `assist` key names, which every label names too.

pages.description: One line per page the record holds a reply for, in page order.

model_words.description: Distinct words of the blocks a swap would write: not a cut last block, furniture `--drop-furniture` leaves out, a table's text outside its cells, or a line the guard leaves out.

engine_words.description: Distinct words of this page in the engine-only Markdown, a table's header row the next page repeats kept (decision #151).

blocks.description: How many of the model's blocks this artifact writes.

left_out.description: What of the reply is left out, by code, sorted; only non-zero codes appear. Blocks: `proposed-table-duplicate-v1`, `proposed-block-truncated-v1`, `proposed-table-unparsed-v1` (a `table` holding no cell, or one whose spans would lay it out on more than 100,000 slots), `proposed-block-not-projected-v1` (off a swapped page, any block but a table, a chart and the caption before one; an empty block; furniture under `--drop-furniture`). Lines: `proposed-value-contradicted-v1`, `proposed-line-unsupported-v1`. In Markdown only, `gfm-span-slots-unrepresentable-v1`: slots a model table's spans covered.
